title: A Letter for the Harbor
premise: Gideon Dravenmoor carries the sealed final dispatch of the Republic of Vellamare — a confession naming the generals who sold the harbor fleet to the enemy — aboard a refugee ship bound for neutral ports. When a meticulous imperial census taker, Corvin Ashe, boards to document passengers, his one question too many unravels her cover and forces an uneasy alliance: he wants accuracy for the record, she wants the truth to survive the victors' historians. Hunted across three port cities by republican loyalists who want the letter destroyed and imperial agents who want it buried, Gideon must choose between protecting her found family of shipmates and delivering the truth. In the end she reads the letter aloud into Corvin's official census ledger — making it, irrevocably, part of the historical record — at the cost of her own name being struck from it.
about_author: Ansel Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the personal papers of displaced civil servants. Their fiction explores what ordinary record-keepers owe to history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Aboard the refugee ship Meridian, Gideon hides the republic's last diplomatic dispatch sewn into her coat lining while mending nets and keeping busy hands. Flashbacks establish her loyalty to the dead envoy who entrusted it to her. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced ordinariness.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. The imperial census taker boards at Port Callis, methodical and unloved, documenting the displaced. His routine questions snag on Gideon's impossible answers — no birthplace, no family, no trade before the war. He lets it go, but writes a marginal note. Emotional beat: the hunter's first, unwitting step.

chapters.title: What the Shipmates Know
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Her found family — cook Maren, engineer Tull, orphaned stowaway Pip — sense something weighs on her. A loyalist passenger recognizes the envoy's seal wax on her sleeve and warns that others aboard serve the generals now. Emotional beat: warmth strained by secrecy.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Letter
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin cross-references passenger manifests and discovers 'Gideon Dravenmoor' died at the fall of the capital. Confronting her privately, he finds not a spy but a terrified courier — and glimpses the seal. He offers silence in exchange for the truth. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Port Callis Burns Its Papers
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Imperial agents arrive to purge the port archives of republican records. Gideon realizes history is being erased in real time; Corvin watches his own careful work fed into fires. They form a fragile pact: get the letter into an official record the empire cannot disown. Emotional beat: shared outrage forging alliance.

chapters.title: The Loyalist's Bargain
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The loyalist faction aboard offers her escape and protection if she surrenders the letter to be destroyed 'for the crew's safety.' Maren and Tull vote to protect the family over the mission; Pip alone sides with Gideon. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Three Ports, One Truth
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Flight inland through occupied territory as both factions close in. Corvin explains the census ledger's legal weight — anything entered and countersigned becomes permanent record, immune to later revision. The plan crystallizes: enter the letter verbatim, witnessed. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: What Pip Carried
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The loyalists strike; Tull is taken hostage and the letter nearly seized. Pip smuggles it out hidden in a child's schoolbook, and Maren, choosing truth at last, covers their escape at terrible cost. Emotional beat: sacrifice transforming loyalty into something larger than secrecy.

chapters.title: The Counting House
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Cornered in the provincial counting house where the master census ledger is kept, Gideon and Corvin face the imperial historian sent to bury the republic's confession. While agents batter the doors, Gideon dictates the letter aloud and Corvin enters every word, countersigning as witnesses — including the historian himself, trapped by his own office's law. Emotional beat: defiant, breathless triumph.

chapters.title: A Name Struck Through
chapters.summary: Resolution, Gideon's POV. Years later, the ledger survives; historians cite the Harbor Confession. Gideon, officially erased, lives quietly as Maren's sister in a fishing village, visited each spring by Corvin and a grown Pip. She keeps busy hands and an unquiet heart, at peace with the trade she made. Emotional beat: bittersweet permanence — the truth endures, anonymous.
